questions.q:
(a) Write 4.06 × 10⁻³ as an ordinary number. [1]
(b) Write 72 500 000 in standard form. [1]
questions.model:
(a) Move the decimal point 3 places to the left: 0.004 06.
(b) 72 500 000 = 7.25 × 10 000 000 = 7.25 × 10⁷.
questions.tip: In standard form the first number must be at least 1 and less than 10: 72.5 × 10⁶ scores 0.

questions.q:
The mass of a parcel is 3.8 kg, correct to the nearest 100 g.
Write down the lower bound and the upper bound of the mass, in grams.
questions.model:
3.8 kg = 3800 g. Half of 100 g is 50 g.
Lower bound = 3750 g, upper bound = 3850 g.
questions.tip: Halve the degree of accuracy (100 g → 50 g) and convert units before you add and subtract.

questions.q:
Do not use a calculator in this question. Give each answer in standard form.
(a) Work out (6.3 × 10⁵) ÷ (9 × 10⁻²). [2]
(b) Work out (2 × 10⁴)³. [1]
questions.model:
(a) 6.3 ÷ 9 = 0.7 and 10⁵ ÷ 10⁻² = 10⁷, so the answer is 0.7 × 10⁷ = 7 × 10⁶.
(b) 2³ = 8 and (10⁴)³ = 10¹², so the answer is 8 × 10¹².
questions.tip: 0.7 × 10⁷ is not in standard form; adjust it to 7 × 10⁶.

questions.q:
A colony of bacteria has a population of 2.4 × 10⁴. The population increases by 15% every hour.
(a) Calculate the population after 6 hours. Give your answer in standard form, correct to 3 significant figures. [2]
(b) Find the number of complete hours until the population first exceeds 1 × 10⁵. [2]
ms: (b) M1: trials showing 2.4 × 10⁴ × 1.15¹⁰ (= 97 100) and 2.4 × 10⁴ × 1.15¹¹ (= 111 700), or equivalent
questions.tip: Show the trial on each side of the target value: that is what earns the method mark.

questions.q:
A metal cube has side length 4.3 cm, correct to the nearest 0.1 cm.
Its mass is 640 g, correct to the nearest 10 g.
Density = mass ÷ volume.
(a) Calculate the upper bound of the density of the metal. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures. [3]
(b) Calculate the lower bound of the density. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures. [2]
(c) Use your answers to (a) and (b) to give the density to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer. [1]
ms: (a) M1: 645 ÷ 4.25³ (their upper mass ÷ their lower side cubed)
(c) B1: 8 g/cm³, because both bounds round to 8 correct to 1 significant figure
questions.model:
(a) Upper mass = 645 g, lower side = 4.25 cm.
Upper density = 645 ÷ 4.25³ = 645 ÷ 76.765… = 8.40 g/cm³.
(b) Lower mass = 635 g, upper side = 4.35 cm.
Lower density = 635 ÷ 4.35³ = 635 ÷ 82.312… = 7.71 g/cm³.
(c) 8 g/cm³ (1 s.f.), because 8.40 and 7.71 both round to 8 to 1 significant figure but not to the same value to 2 significant figures.
questions.tip: For a division, the upper bound is (biggest top) ÷ (smallest bottom).

questions.q:
(a) A boat loses 8% of its value every year. After 3 years it is worth €38 934.40.
Calculate the value of the boat when it was new. [2]
(b) Kai invests €10 000 at r% per year compound interest. After 5 years the investment is worth €12 166.53.
Find the value of r. [3]
ms: (b) M1: (12 166.53 ÷ 10 000)^(1/5) or ⁵√1.216653 (allow trial and improvement reaching 1.04)
questions.tip: Reverse depreciation: divide by the multiplier to the power of the number of years; never add 8% back three times.
